name: C-arm Flat-Detector CT Parenchymal Blood Volume maps
domain: Cerebral Infaction and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia
description: C-arm flat-detector computed tomography (FDCT) parenchymal blood volume (PBV) maps are an imaging technique used to estimate blood volume within brain tissue. A C-arm angiography system captures rotational images before and during intravenous contrast administration. The images are then processed to generate voxel-based maps of parenchymal blood volume. Following aSAH, areas of substantially reduced PBV may indicate severely ischemic or infarcted brain tissue.

name: Negative ultraslow potential
domain: Cerebral Infaction and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia
description: A negative ultraslow potential (NUP) is a large, prolonged negative shift in the brain's electrical potential that can occur when brain cells progressively lose their ability to recover from ischemic injury. As the injury becomes irreversible, brain cells die and tissue damage accumulates. NUP can be detected through continuous electrocorticography (ECoG), using electrodes placed directly on the surface of the brain. Following aSAH, NUP has been proposed as an electrophysiological marker of irreversible brain tissue injury and developing cerebral infarction, potentially identifying infarction while it is evolving rather than only after it becomes visible on conventional imaging.
source: Identified through the cerebral infaction scoping review
